subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - latency & throughput SLOs
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-07-20T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: performance targets & next steps

Thanks for the demo earlier — it was helpful. Quick recap from our side and the specific performance targets we need to validate before procurement can move forward:

- P95 latency target: <= 150ms for typical completions (~<=256 tokens)
- Sustained throughput: ~1,000 requests/min (spiky bursts to ~1,500)
- Concurrent sessions: up to 50 concurrent user streams
- Streaming: must support partial responses (chunked streaming) with low first-byte latency
- Availability SLO: 99.9% for the inference endpoint

Attached is a sample workload CSV from our production traces and the call recording for reference. Our initial ask: can Redwood run a dedicated-capacity performance validation that mirrors this workload and confirm recommended GPU type and reserved throughput sizing for these SLOs?

Next steps we need from Redwood:
1) Recommended GPU family & cluster sizing (e.g., # H100 vs # A100) for the targets above
2) Description of the validation plan (synthetic + replay using our traces) and proposed dates
3) Any limitations on streaming or KV caching that would affect first-byte latency
4) Estimated cost range for the reserved/dev validation window

Preferred timing: we'd like to run tests before month-end if possible. Procurement will need a short statement of work and a ballpark quote to prepare internal approval.

Thanks,
Alex
Director of ML Engineering
Acme AI

Attachments: call-recording-20260720.mp3 (audio/mpeg); workload-sample.csv (text/csv)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance targets & next steps

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and the workload sample. This is exactly the sort of info we need to size a Dedicated validation. High level answers up front, then a proposed plan: 

1) Recommended GPUs & sizing - For the targets you listed (short responses, heavy concurrency + streaming), our starting recommendation is H100-based nodes for headroom (better FP16/Transformer kernel performance and streaming efficiency). Practically: 2x H100 (reserved cluster) should comfortably hit ~1,000 req/min and 50 concurrent streams for models in the 7–34B class depending on batching. If you prefer a more cost-optimized option, 4x A100-s setup is a viable alternative but provides less single-request headroom for low-latency streaming.

2) Expected ballpark performance (approx, will validate):
- 1x H100 (single node) - p95 ~ 120–180ms at low concurrency for <256 tokens (varies by model & pipeline)
- 2x H100 (reserved cluster with routing + prefix cache) - expected p95 ~ 80–120ms at 50 concurrent streams with reserved throughput and modest batching (we'll tune batching thresholds to prioritize latency)

3) Streaming & caching - Our runtime supports chunked streaming. First-byte latencies are affected by kernel startup and batching windows; we'll run tests with aggressive min_batch=1 behavior to minimize first-byte time and enable prefix/KV caching when beneficial. We'll surface exact measured first-byte p50/p95 in the report.

4) Validation plan & dates
- Phase A (synthetic microbench): baseline on 1xH100 and 1xA100 to compare kernels and cold-start behavior (1 day)
- Phase B (replay): run your workload-sample.csv and production traces against 2xH100 and 4xA100 configurations (2 days)
- Phase C (tuning): iterate config (batching, routing policy, kv cache) and produce final metrics + SLO recommendation (1 day)

Proposed test window: 2026-07-27 to 2026-07-29 (let us know if you need earlier). We'll provide a short benchmark report with p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and tail latencies, throughput curves, and recommended reserved throughput.

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-plan.pdf (application/pdf)

Action items:
- Please confirm the test window above or propose alternatives
- Share any compliance/networking guardrails we need for Private/Dedicated (VPC IP allowlist, dataset redaction notes)
- Procurement: if you can share the procurement timeline we can include a ballpark quote in the validation SOW

I'll loop Marissa and Aditya to own the run and sizing details.

—Rafael
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
